correctness.summary: Nash-Williams reduces the claim to induced-set density inequalities. The two-parameter excess inequality is proved for all relative positions of the subset sizes, one-sided subsets are controlled separately, low-ceiling cases are handled directly, and the total-cycle-rank-eight obstruction is checked exactly.

limitations: The criterion is sufficient, not necessary.
The quadratic threshold for each fixed full-set ceiling at least four is not claimed optimal.
No claim is made about maximizing fractional arboricity.
Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from very recent or unindexed parallel work.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The directly relevant 2026 join-arboricity preprint was inspected and gives only general bounds plus examples. Exact and synonymous searches using join/sum/cone and cycle-rank/cyclomatic/circuit-rank/corank terminology found no theorem covering the stated full-set criterion or its sharp universal threshold-eight obstruction.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result gives an exact join-arboricity formula under a cycle-rank criterion whose allowance grows quadratically with the predicted arboricity, and it identifies total cycle rank seven as the largest possible universal constant.
